rule_summary: The law sets no minimum age for foster carers. Socialstyrelsen says carers need to be over 18, secure in themselves and leading an orderly life.
notes: Min insats FAQ (page dated 22 May 2024). The Social Services Act only requires the home to be investigated.

rule_summary: Many councils ask for carers of at least 25. Stockholm and Örebro say over 25 or at least 25. Skellefteå says carers should be past 25. Uppsala prefers 25 to 65 and Piteå 25 to 60.
notes: Local practice, not a national rule. Malmö says age does not decide and judges maturity instead. Humana and Startsteget (private providers) say there is no age limit.

rule_summary: A person must be 18 or over to adopt.
notes: Children and Parents Code; text amended up to SFS 2026:1603. Stockholm's adoption page says the same.

rule_summary: There is no upper age limit. The council makes an overall judgement of the person's life and circumstances, and age is one factor in it.
notes: Some councils set their own ranges (see se-se-min_age-2). Humana says carers should be able to be there until the young person is past 20.

rule_summary: The law sets no upper age. When deciding on consent to adopt from abroad, the social committee must take particular account of the applicant's age and health.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652.

rule_summary: General advice: the investigator should look at whether the applicant's age matters for the overall judgement. The advice gives examples: health, the age gap between applicant and child, and any existing relationship between them.
notes: MFoF's general advice on handling intercountry adoption cases. MFoF says it has not yet been updated for the 2025 Social Services Act. No fixed age gap is stated.

rule_summary: Single people and couples can foster. Socialstyrelsen says a single carer can be best for some children, while others need several adults.
notes: Malmö says no partner is needed. Trollhättan welcomes single people and same-sex couples. When there are two carers, both are investigated (see se-se-home_study-3).

rule_summary: Spouses and cohabiting partners may only adopt together, and no one else may adopt jointly. A single person may adopt. A spouse or partner may adopt the other's child with their consent.
notes: Stockholm's adoption page lists married people, registered partners, cohabiting couples and single people.

rule_summary: There are no barriers to fostering because of sexual orientation, gender identity or religion. Religion can matter when matching a child to a home.

There is no national language rule. Socialstyrelsen says carers must be able to deal with the municipality and others in the child's life. So, it says, Swedish matters, and speaking the child's language can help.
notes: Many councils ask for good Swedish: Stockholm, Uppsala, Linköping and Örebro; Lund asks for fluent spoken and written Swedish.

rule_summary: Carers can work full time. A carer may need to stay at home part or full time, depending on the child's age and needs. If social services need a carer to take leave, they pay for the lost income.
notes: Malmö and Stockholm ask carers to have an occupation. Some councils' contracted homes need a carer at home full time (for example Västerås and Kristianstad).

rule_summary: A child's needs may mean that a carer must give up other work for a time. In that case SKR advises setting the extra pay as a raised fee (förhöjt arvode), not as separate pay for lost earnings. The decision and agreement should say why, for how long and when it will be reviewed.
notes: SKR circular 26:33, dated 26 October 2026. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: There is no income requirement. Socialstyrelsen says the home should live an orderly and stable life.
notes: Stockholm and Uppsala ask for stable finances or income; Malmö says it judges stability, not income.

rule_summary: No formal qualification is needed. Councils give carers the training their task needs.
notes: Luleå's page; Piteå and Västerås say the same. Luleå wants someone in an emergency home to have experience or training with children.

rule_summary: General advice: the investigation should look at whether each carer has the health, mental stability and stamina the task needs.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends. Linköping and Stockholm ask for good health; Uppsala for stable health and the ability to work.

rule_summary: Applicants give a health declaration and a medical certificate early in the home study. If a condition could affect parenting, they should give a specialist's statement; for mental health, from a psychiatrist or licensed psychologist.
notes: MFoF's general advice. MFoF's adoption process page also lists references and a medical certificate.

rule_summary: There is no national rule on owning or renting. Councils read say a house or a flat, in town or the country, is fine.
notes: Linköping's page; Uppsala says house or flat does not matter. Uppsala asks for stable housing and that carers live within driving distance of Uppsala.

rule_summary: General advice: the investigation should look at whether the child can have a room of their own. The same goes for a safe and secure environment and a stimulating free time.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends.

rule_summary: There must be room for a child in the home. Socialstyrelsen says a room of their own matters to many children, but needs differ by age and child.
notes: Most councils and providers read ask for the child's own room: Stockholm, Lund, Trollhättan, Skellefteå and Humana. Uppsala adds that no one in the family should give up their room. Lund and Humana want every child already at home to have their own room. Malmö says very young children do not need one at first.

rule_summary: There is no national limit on children per home in the texts read. Several councils and providers ask that the family's own children are over 3.
notes: The value is the age of own children asked for. Stockholm and Humana say no child under 3 at home; Uppsala says none aged 3 or under; Luleå asks this for emergency homes.

rule_summary: No national smoking rule was found. GFO in Västernorrland covers health, smoking and alcohol in its joint interview with the adults.
No national driving rule was found. Kristianstad asks contracted emergency homes for a driving licence and a car.
notes: Local practice for one kind of home.

rule_summary: A child may not be placed in a foster home without a decision on care. The social committee may not decide without a social committee having investigated the home and the conditions for care in it. The same applies to emergency homes.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. SOSFS 2012:11 has the investigation judge the home's general suitability and, when a child is in mind, that child's needs. The basis for a placement decision must include a current family home investigation (4 kap. 1 §, 5 kap. 1 §).

rule_summary: The investigation must cover the family's make-up, background, life situation and habits, and the home and surroundings. It must also cover each carer's personal qualities and capacity to care, and their attitude to the task. It must pay special attention to violence, other crime or substance misuse that could put a child at risk.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends.

rule_summary: The investigation must include interviews, home visits and references. Where there are two carers, they are interviewed both apart and together. The findings are put together in a written family home investigation.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends.

rule_summary: Socialstyrelsen offers two standard methods: BRA-fam for the first assessment of people who register interest, and Familjehemsvinjetter later in the investigation. It also publishes a process description (Pro-fam).
notes: Page updated 9 September 2026. Luleå and GFO say they use BRA-fam. We did not find BBIC (Barns behov i centrum) named as the method for assessing carers. BBIC is used for the child's own case (not yet checked).

rule_summary: A child living abroad may not be taken in for adoption without the social committee's consent (medgivande). The committee gives consent if the applicant is suitable. It looks at knowledge and insight about adopted children, personal qualities and social network, and age and health. It also looks at the stability of a couple's relationship.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. The home study (medgivandeutredning) is done by the social committee where the applicant lives (24 kap. 6 §).

rule_summary: In the home study the investigator looks at relationships and social network, background, work, age, and physical and mental health. The study also covers beliefs, motives, finances, housing and attitude to the child's background. The report is then sent abroad as the applicants' presentation.
notes: MFoF's page on the adoption process. A refusal can be appealed to the administrative court.

rule_summary: References for each prospective carer must come from at least two people who are independent of each other. General advice: both people close to the carer and people who know them through work.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends.

rule_summary: Other municipalities may have had children placed in the home in the last five years. If so, the committee must ask them for references on each carer, with the carer's consent.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends.

rule_summary: Before placing a child in a foster home or emergency home, the social committee must check the people it means to use. It must get information on them from the criminal records register and the suspicion register.
notes: Socialtjänstförordning (2025:468), the Social Services Ordinance in force from 1 July 2025; text amended up to SFS 2026:1868.

rule_summary: General advice: with consent, the committee should also get register information from the Enforcement Authority (Kronofogden, for debts) and the Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan).
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends. Many councils also check the Transport Agency's register of people taken into custody for drunkenness (LOB), for example Malmö, Norrköping, Luleå and GFO. GFO asks applicants to order the extracts themselves.

rule_summary: If the home is in the same municipality, the committee must check its own social services register. General advice: with consent, also ask social services in every municipality the carer has lived in during the last five years.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends. The value is the look-back period in the general advice. Kristianstad lets applicants order their own social services extract online with BankID.

rule_summary: In the home study the investigator checks whether the applicant is known in social services registers. The investigator also asks for extracts from the police suspicion and criminal records registers.
The social committee must provide the training needed by the people it plans to use as foster carers or emergency carers.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. GFO says councils have had this duty since 1 January 2013, under the earlier Act.

rule_summary: Socialstyrelsen has a basic course for foster and emergency carers, Ett hem att växa i (A home to grow up in). It is meant for every kind of placement. A new edition of the carers' book came out on 8 December 2025.
notes: Min insats says most municipalities offer it. The law does not name the course or set hours. Linköping calls it obligatory; Uppsala, Nyköping, Jämtland and NEB-teamet say all their carers take it; GFO offers it free. A digital extra course is for carers who already know the child (nätverkshem).

rule_summary: Linköping's basic course runs over eight sessions before a person becomes a carer.
notes: Local practice, not a national rule.

rule_summary: Before consent to adopt from abroad, applicants must have attended a parent education course chosen by the committee. People who have adopted from abroad before may get consent without it.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. MFoF coordinates the course, keeps the national material and lists the providers; the municipality directs applicants to one.

rule_summary: A municipality may charge a reasonable fee, no higher than its own costs, for parent education before adoption.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. The fee charged was not checked.

rule_summary: General advice: the committee should make sure carers get supervision and further training suited to the task.
notes: Socialstyrelsen's regulations and general advice SOSFS 2012:11, as amended by HSLF-FS 2025:24 from 1 July 2025. This is the consolidated web version. The printed text is the one that counts. Regulations (föreskrifter) bind; general advice (allmänna råd) recommends. No set number of hours was found.

rule_summary: An emergency home (jourhem) takes children for short stays again and again. A child may stay there at most two months after social services finish their investigation, unless there are special reasons.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. Councils also name contracted emergency homes, reinforced foster homes and treatment foster homes; these are local types, not set in law.

rule_summary: A private organisation can propose foster and emergency homes to social services and support them (a consultant agency, konsulentverksamhet). To do this, it needs a permit from the Health and Social Care Inspectorate (IVO).
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. Socialstyrelsen's HSLF-FS 2018:2 sets quality rules for these agencies. Their carers are investigated in the same way as other foster homes (Socialstyrelsen, search result).

rule_summary: When a child must live away from home, the committee must first consider whether someone close to the child can take them in. What is best for the child always decides.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. A home for a child the carers already know is called a network home (nätverkshem). Socialstyrelsen says it is investigated the same way as other foster homes.

rule_summary: Consent to adopt from abroad lapses if the child has not come into the applicant's care within three years.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. Applicants can then apply for a new consent (MFoF).

rule_summary: Applicants must tell the committee about any major change while consent is valid. If no child has been proposed within two years, the committee checks whether things have changed. Consent is withdrawn if the conditions are no longer met.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652.

rule_summary: The law sets no time limit for the family home investigation. Luleå says it takes 4 to 6 months; Örebro says it usually runs over several months.
notes: Local statements, not a national rule.

rule_summary: When a child has been proposed, the committee must decide quickly whether the adoption may go on, and within two weeks of being told. The time can be longer only for exceptional reasons.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. MFoF says waiting times for a child vary by country and are known by the adoption organisation.

rule_summary: Carers can live in another municipality. Before placing a child in a home elsewhere, the committee must inform and consult that municipality.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. Socialstyrelsen says people can register interest with any municipality, not only their own. Some councils want carers nearby, for example Uppsala.

rule_summary: Consent to adopt from abroad is given by the social committee of the municipality responsible for the applicant.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. MFoF says people apply to the social committee where they live.

rule_summary: SKR's recommended basic expense allowance for 2026 for a child aged 0 to 12 is SEK 5,427 a month. This is 110% of the price base amount. It includes child benefit, which is deducted when paid to the carer.
notes: SKR circular 25:52, dated 3 November 2025, read from a copy on Vårgårda Municipality's site (the file name says 25-39). With extra costs, the tax-free total can reach SEK 7,647 a month. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: SKR's recommended basic expense allowance for 2026 for a young person aged 13 to 19 is SEK 6,167 a month. This is 125% of the price base amount.
notes: SKR circular 25:52, read from Vårgårda's copy. With extra costs, the tax-free total can reach SEK 8,633 a month. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: SKR's recommended basic fee (grundarvode) for 2026 is SEK 12,230 a month per child aged 0 to 19. Example raised fees go up to SEK 18,779.
notes: SKR circular 25:52, read from Vårgårda's copy. The fee rose 3.5% on 2025. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: SKR's recommended basic expense allowance for 2027 for a child aged 0 to 12 is SEK 5,463 a month. It is based on the 2027 price base amount of SEK 59,600.
notes: SKR circular 26:33, dated 26 October 2026 and published 27 November 2026; its title says 2026 but its tables are for 2027. With extra costs, the tax-free total can reach SEK 7,698 a month. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: SKR's recommended basic expense allowance for 2027 for a young person aged 13 to 19 is SEK 6,208 a month.
notes: SKR circular 26:33. With extra costs, the tax-free total can reach SEK 8,692 a month. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: SKR's recommended basic fee for 2027 is SEK 12,634 a month per child aged 0 to 19, up 3.3%. Example raised fees go up to SEK 19,399.
notes: SKR circular 26:33. SKR's recommendations are not law: each municipality sets the pay in its agreement with the carer. Expenses are tax-free up to set limits; the fee is taxed as income.

rule_summary: Carers are paid in two parts: an expense allowance for the child's costs and a fee for the task. The fee is taxed and counts towards sickness benefit and pension, but not occupational pension or unemployment insurance. Amounts follow SKR's recommendations and vary by municipality and the child's age.
notes: SKR says carers are commissioned by the social committee, not employed. Carers can deduct expense allowance above SEK 5,000 a year in their tax return (SKR page).

rule_summary: MFoF lists steps for after the child arrives. They include telling the social committee, registering the child, a medical check, child health services, Försäkringskassan and an adoption grant (adoptionsbidrag).
notes: The amount and rules of the adoption grant were not checked.

rule_summary: When a child is placed, the committee must make an agreement with the carers. It sets out what the committee and the carers will each do for the child's protection and support.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652.

rule_summary: Support after placement: the committee must give carers the advice, support and other help they need. It must also follow the care closely through regular visits and talks with the child.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. Councils describe a named family home social worker, group supervision, and in Malmö an evening and weekend helpline. 22 kap. 11 § gets new wording on 1 January 2027.

rule_summary: A child may have lived in the same foster home for two years. If so, the committee must consider applying to move custody to the carers. After that, it must consider it every year.
notes: Socialtjänstlag (2025:400), the Social Services Act in force from 1 July 2025; consolidated text amended up to SFS 2026:1652. If custody moves, the municipality may keep paying the new guardians reasonable pay (22 kap. 15 §). Some council pages still say three years.

rule_summary: Only organisations authorised under the Act may mediate adoptions from abroad, and adopters must use one. MFoF may allow an adoption without an organisation in single cases, for example a relative's child.
notes: Text amended up to SFS 2025:419. MFoF's page (updated 10 September 2026) says only two organisations hold authorisation: Adoptionscentrum, which mediates, and Barnen Framför Allt, which is winding down.

rule_summary: A ban on intercountry adoption mediation is under discussion. MFoF says the government has not yet set a timetable for a possible ban, and people in a queue should ask their adoption organisation.
notes: MFoF answer updated 5 May 2026. A related MFoF answer mentions the Adoption Commission's report (Adoptionskommissionen); search results name it SOU 2025:61, Sveriges internationella adoptionsverksamhet (not yet checked).
